title: Rabana (Sri Lankan floor drum)
summary: The rabana is a broad, flat frame drum of Sri Lanka, so large that it is laid on the floor. Players sit round it and strike the skin with their palms in turn, and the pattern travels from one player to the next. The centre gives a deep boom and each quarter of the skin has its own voice.
howToPlay: Five places on the skin are lit: the centre, called Dum, and four quarters named North, East, South and West, one for each player round the drum.
A ring closes on a place when its stroke is due. Strike that place just as the ring meets the skin.
Start with the slow round, then try the quickening round, where the pace rises and the centre answers.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through.
The strokes pass round the circle in the order North, East, South, West, with the centre as the answer.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of New Year play, not transcriptions.
heritageNote: Rabana playing is a social pastime at the Sinhala and Tamil New Year in Sri Lanka, when families gather round the drum and take turns to strike in a quickening rhythm.
